topic: Olbers' paradox — why the night sky is dark

fact_check.claim: In an infinite, static, eternal universe every line of sight would end on a stellar surface and the sky would be bright; the observed darkness is explained mainly by the finite age of the universe (~13.8 billion years) and cosmic expansion/redshift.
fact_check.source_hint: Standard cosmology texts on Olbers' paradox; NASA/ESA cosmology age estimates. Note that redshift and finite stellar lifetimes are contributing factors, finite age is the dominant one.

hooks: The night sky should be as bright as the Sun.
Why is space black? Not because there are no stars.
'Infinite' is the word that breaks the sky.
titles: The Night Sky Should Be Blindingly Bright. Why Isn't It?
Darkness Is Proof The Universe Has An Age
Olbers' Paradox: The Simple Question That Broke Cosmology

beats.vo: The night sky should be as bright as the Sun.
beats.visual: Real night sky that instantly blows out to white; hard flash on frame 1

beats.vo: If the universe is infinite and eternal, every direction ends on a star.
beats.visual: Animated sight-lines shooting out from the viewer into a dense star field

beats.vo: Even a distant star is a tiny disk of light. Stack enough of them and the whole sky glows. This is Olbers' paradox.
beats.visual: Shells of stars stacking outward, brightness meter climbing to white

beats.vo: So the darkness isn't empty space. It's a clue about time.
beats.visual: White sky snaps back to black; a clock icon appears

beats.vo: And the fix isn't 'stars are too far'. That doesn't help.
beats.visual: 'TOO FAR' stamped and crossed out in red

beats.vo: The universe is about 13.8 billion years old. Light from farther away simply hasn't arrived yet. On top of that, expansion stretches that light into infrared our eyes can't see.
beats.visual: Expanding sphere with an outer dark rim; visible light stretching into red

beats.vo: You're not looking at emptiness. You're looking at the edge of how far light has travelled.
beats.visual: Slow push back into the same night sky from frame 1
Identical composition to frame 1, seamless loop

payoff: Darkness is a horizon in time, not an absence of stars.
cta: Void or horizon — which word fits the night sky?
pinned_comment: Void or horizon? One word 👇 (And should I do the 'why is anything here at all' follow-up? A or B)
description:
The night sky should be as bright as the surface of the Sun. It isn't — and the reason isn't a lack of stars.

In an infinite, eternal universe, every line of sight would eventually hit a star. The sky is dark because the universe is ~13.8 billion years old: light from farther away hasn't reached us, and expansion redshifts much of the rest.

Void or horizon — which word fits?

Concept: Olbers' paradox / finite age of the universe. Educational summary.
